title: Scheduler, tasks, events
summary: The scheduler is the best-engineered subsystem in this tree in the sense that matters: its invariants are checked rather than trusted - one 24-byte frame and one resume path, a slice layout written once in SCH_PARTITION and derived by macro with %error guards, a canary compared on every switch including task 0's, an unconditional 0xCC high-water fill and a death panel naming the culprit, a guarded hlt with two separately-reasoned lost-wakeup guards, exact 32-bit PIT accounting, and a ROM-chain private stack that survives stack-hopping BIOSes. The code defects are small: task_spawn's IF=0 window silently grew to include the slice fill (~676 us at 384 bytes), sch_rhook leaks IF=1 on its skip path on kern_big (0-byte fix: take the sti only after the skip tests and the lock raise), evq_push wakes before it copies (0-byte reorder), the two private ISR stacks have no canary and sit back to back, and the STKDIAG instrument that sized them scans from the wrong end. The real weakness is prose: about forty statements across sched.inc, events.inc, stkdiag.inc, SPEC.md 7/8/10/20.6, apps/os88api.inc and KERNEL-MEMORY.md describe replaced designs - including the SDK still telling package authors a worker gets DS = ES = CS = KERNEL_SEG while SPEC.md 20.6 says that was fixed, kern_small's slot count (7 vs 5), and an unresolved kernel-wide contradiction about whether .bss arrives zeroed (which sched_init already depends on: nothing ever stores sch_chbusy). Against prior art the one systemic gap is that a task can block only on time: every other wait is a sleep-poll or a yield-spin, and sch_wake_ui is a one-task special case of a missing per-task wake; an AmigaOS-Signal / SysV-wakeup style task_wake with a sticky pending bit is ~25-30 resident bytes and an additive cell, and is the change of model worth making. A one-shot UI wake boost (~22 bytes) is the cheap form of the priority every peer (OS/2, GEOS, AmigaOS) gave its interactive thread, to be taken only if a two-worker measurement moves.

strengths.title: One frame format, one resume path, one frame builder
strengths.why: sch_isr, task_yield and task_spawn all produce the frame sch_resume pops, and sch_frame is the single body both task_spawn and the compactor's worker restart call, so two paths that must agree word for word cannot drift.

strengths.title: The slice layout is data written once
strengths.why: SCH_PARTITION expands into the counters/asserts, sch_stkbase and sch_stksize; ascending order (first fit = smallest fit), evenness, minimum size, count and total are build-time errors. This is the pattern every hand-mirrored table should copy.

strengths.title: Thin stacks are checked, not trusted
strengths.why: Canary on every switch away including task 0, unconditional 0xCC fill at spawn so the shipping kernel's high water is readable on the field machine, and a death panel that moves off the dead stack first and prints slot, SP and instance name.

strengths.title: Race-correct idle and UI blocking
strengths.why: sch_wake_ui's one-word store feeds two lost-wakeup guards, each test-halt-clear in one IF=0 window with STI's shadow covering hlt; the masked-IRQ0 fail-safe spins instead of hanging; every READY-making event posts sch_idlewake and the fallback spends it.

strengths.title: Exact per-task accounting at negligible cost
strengths.why: 32-bit [ticks]:phase stamps with the IRR coherence test, charged only on a real change, paused rather than wrong under sub-ticks - no peer of the period had exact per-task CPU time.

strengths.title: The ROM is fenced
strengths.why: The int 08h chain runs on a private stack only when SS is ours, sch_switch refuses to park a foreign SS, and a nested tick accounts and wakes but never switches - correct paranoia for an OS calling int 13h/16h with IF=1 on unknown BIOSes.

strengths.title: Run-time mode switch with no rendezvous
strengths.why: Pre-emptive and cooperative share every byte of state and the watchdog re-arms on every entry to sch_switch; no historical peer let the user flip this live.

strengths.title: Event ring policy
strengths.why: Drop-oldest with the EVT_WAKE promise exception, wm_wake's own full-ring refusal, bounded per-pass drain and the wheel as a level - Mac OS PostEvent also dropped the oldest; os8088 adds the promise exception.

strengths.title: Word-as-two-bytes tricks are guarded at the declaration
strengths.why: Every paired store (uiwake/idlewake, idleslot/top, rbusy/lock, fast/fcnt, T_INST/T_FLAGS, spl_busy/spl_quiet) has an %error, so a reorder of .bss fails the build instead of the machine.

findings.title: task_spawn holds IF=0 across the whole 0xCC slice fill
findings.detail: The cli at task_spawn's head covers the rep stosw of the entire slice. PERFORMANCE.md measures RAM rep stosw at 1.76 us/byte, so a 384 slice is ~676 us at IF=0 (338 us at 192) plus ~30 stores. The window was priced when the fill was KFZ-only and never re-priced: the routine header and SPEC.md 8 still say '~30 stores with no I/O' (the fill's own comment, sched.inc:972-976, does admit 'a few hundred microseconds' and 'runs inside the spawn's cli'). 676 us is ~4 lost pulses of a 5.5 kHz speaker-sample ISR (SPEC.md 34.11.3 counts each 864-cycle IF=0 stretch as one) and two-thirds of a 9600-baud UART byte; spawns happen at every launch and every SB stream open (the transient refill/drain tasks).
evidence: kernel/sched.inc:983-989 rep stosw of the slice inside the window
findings.recommendation: Reserve the slot under the cli (T_STATE = 3, which the wake loop and scan ignore and every T_STATE!=0 reader treats as occupied; zero T_FLAGS in the same store), popf/pushf back to the caller's IF, fill and build the frame, then cli for the sch_top raise and the publish. Check first that no snapshot reader (the Task Manager's SS_TSTATE copy) shows a package the new value 3, or document it. Fix the two '~30 stores' sentences regardless.
findings.verify_note: Re-read task_spawn (sched.inc:902-1053): pushf/cli at 914-915 is not undone until .done's popf, and the rep stosw at 989 runs inside. T_STATE readers outside sched.inc (instance.inc:682,707; mega.inc:380,4226) compare with 0 or 2, so a reserved 3 reads as occupied and not sleeping; the remaining risk is a published snapshot showing 3, added to the recommendation.

findings.title: sch_rhook returns IF=1 on its skip path under a sample ISR (kern_big)
findings.detail: sch_rhook sti's when [spk_seg] is open before its three skip tests; the taken path re-cli's but the skip path rets with IF=1, against its own 'out: ... IF=0' and sch_isr's 'IF=0 throughout ... never sti'. On the .full call the rest of the tick (sch_account, snd_tick and DSV_TICK - which SPEC.md 8.7.5 says runs at IF=0 - and the wake loop) runs interruptible, deepening nesting on sch_chstack. It does not reach sch_switch, since each skip reason independently refuses the switch (chbusy -> .tres, rbusy implies the hook raised sch_lock -> .tres, foreign SS -> sch_switch's own test). On the .rate call the skip path goes straight to sch_resume under a sample ISR, so only the .full call matters.
evidence: kernel/sched.inc:624-627 cli only on the taken path
findings.recommendation: Move the `cmp word [spk_seg], 0 / je / sti` block from the head to just after the `add word [sch_rbusy], 0x0101` (skip tests and lock raise at IF=0, then the sti, then the call): 0 bytes, the skip path never sti's, and the tests are tens of clocks against the 864-cycle pulse budget. Do NOT take the reorder `KDS / sub word [sch_rbusy],0x0101 / .skip: cli / ret`: it leaves one instruction boundary at IF=1 with the lock already lowered, where a nested tick could switch away from inside this ISR - the thing sch_rhook raises sch_lock to prevent.
findings.verify_note: Bug confirmed by reading sch_rhook (sched.inc:594-627) and both call sites. The reviewer's fix was wrong: lowering sch_rbusy/sch_lock before the cli opens a window where a nested IRQ0 (a speaker pulse chaining into sch_isr) sees sch_lock = 0 at IF=1 and can reach sch_switch inside the outer ISR. Replaced with the sti-after-the-tests reorder.

findings.title: sch_lock has become a general Forbid, and yield/sleep/gfx_lock silently degrade under it
findings.detail: SPEC.md 7 says exactly two routines raise sch_lock; the tree raises it in disk.inc, diskw.inc, memory.inc, xmem.inc, fsx.inc, hiber.inc, mega.inc, megados.inc and snd.inc. Under it task_yield self-resumes, so a gfx_lock owned by another task spins for ever, and task_sleep stores T_STATE=2 and returns at once, leaving a running task marked sleeping until the next unlocked switch applies the sleep late. memory.inc dropping the lock around a park shows the rule is known; nothing states or enforces it. AmigaOS's Forbid had the same counter and defined Wait() inside it by saving the nest count per task.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite SPEC.md 7's paragraph to describe sch_lock as a nestable pre-emption-off bracket with its holder list, and state beside it that nothing inside may yield, sleep or take gfx_lock (doc fix below). Optionally make task_sleep a no-op under the lock (cmp byte [sch_lock],0 / jne before the state store) and add a knob assertion in task_yield's locked arm.
findings.prior_art: AmigaOS Exec Forbid/Permit (TDNestCnt saved per task so Wait() inside Forbid is legal)
findings.verify_note: grep of `inc byte [sch_lock]` finds raisers in all the listed files plus mega.inc (a dozen sites); task_yield's .save jumps to sch_isr.sres while it is set; task_sleep stores T_STATE=2 then calls task_yield, which returns at once under the lock.

findings.title: OSAPI_TASK_SLEEP on the UI task ends at the next input, undocumented
findings.detail: sch_wake_ui stores T_STATE=1 unconditionally on every event, mouse byte and keystroke. Window callbacks run on the UI task (all but a W_PAINT a worker's repaint dispatches), so a callback that sleeps for a timed effect is cut short by the next input; the cell says only 'AX = ticks to sleep'.
evidence: kernel/ui.inc:1173-1174 the only intended UI sleep
findings.recommendation: Document on the cell: on the UI task the sleep ends at the first input; loop on OSAPI_GET_TICKS for a minimum. (The cell's %define comment is in abilock's fingerprint: abilock --update, no PKG_FMT bump.) If ever needed, a distinct state for .idle's block lets sch_wake_ui promote only that one (~+8).
findings.verify_note: sch_wake_ui (sched.inc:700-723) writes [sch_tasks+T_STATE] = 1 with no state test; callers include evq_push and kbm_isr. Wording narrowed: not every callback runs on the UI task (SPEC.md 20.6 W_PAINT).

findings.title: task_sleep's range is 1..32768 and unstated
findings.detail: The wake test is the sign of [ticks] - T_WAKE, so AX = 32769..65535 is already 'past' and wakes at the next tick, as do AX = 0 and AX = 1. A package sleeping 'an hour' gets 55 ms.
findings.recommendation: State 1..32768 (0 and 1 both mean the next tick) on the cell and in SPEC.md 8; the cell comment is fingerprinted (abilock --update without a bump).
findings.verify_note: Worked the js test: with T_WAKE = t0 + AX, the scan at t0 + k sees k - AX; AX = 0x8000 stays negative until k = 0x8000, so 32768 works exactly, and 0x8001..0xFFFF read positive at once. The reviewer's 0..32767 / '0x8000 wakes early' was off by one.

findings.title: evq_push wakes the UI task before the record is in the ring
findings.detail: sch_wake_ui is called before pushf/cli. Today's producers are safe (mouse ISR at IF=0, wm_wake under its own cli, kbm_post on the UI task itself), but the routine's contract admits a task-context caller with IF=1, for whom a pre-emption between wake and copy lets the UI task spend sch_uiwake on an empty ring and sleep a tick - the failure SPEC.md 8.1.2.3 exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Move the call to just after the cli.
findings.verify_note: Read evq_push (events.inc:83-158) and ui.inc:1158-1182: the UI task spends sch_uiwake at .woke and sleeps on the next .idle, so a wake that precedes its record by a pre-emption is lost until the tick. sch_wake_ui is two stores and safe at IF=0.

findings.title: The two private ISR stacks have no canary and sit back to back
findings.detail: sch_chstack hosts code the kernel does not own - the ROM's int 08h, its int 1Ch chain, whatever nests in the ROM's sti window, and possibly a DOS program's int 1Ch hook when the tick lands with SS=LOW_SEG. On the built kern_big map mou_pstack is at LOW_SEG:06D6..0756 and sch_chstack starts at 0756, so a chain overflow writes the top of the mouse ISR's stack, which is live exactly when a mouse IRQ nests in the ROM's window. Every task slice has a canary; these two do not.
evidence: kernel/sched.inc:80-89 SCH_CHSTK sizing from measured ROMs
findings.recommendation: Put SCH_MAGIC at sch_chstack's bottom and check it once per TICK, right after the chain's `mov sp, bx` (cmp word [ss:sch_chstack], SCH_MAGIC / jne to a panel that names the chain stack rather than the outgoing task), not in sch_switch on every switch. The seed cannot go in sched_init's .ovl on kern_big, which is 5,119 of its 5,120-byte bound (kernel.asm:8942) - put it in a resident init, or in the room sched-12 frees. The mouse area should guard mou_pstack the same way.
findings.verify_note: Adjacency confirmed on build/kernel.map. Corrected: the reviewer's 'seed in the overlay, free' does not fit (.ovl is 0x13FF = 5,119 bytes against the 512-rounded bound of 5,120), a check in sch_switch is a hot-path cost on every switch (and t_hotpar parity), and sch_stkdie would blame the outgoing task. A per-tick check after the chain is cheaper and names the right culprit.

findings.title: STKDIAG's private-stack high waters scan from the wrong end
findings.detail: sd_cwater and sd_mwater scan down from the top for the first byte still equal to the 0xE5 sentinel, so any byte written during the deepest excursion that happens to be 0xE5 stops the scan early, as does any unwritten gap (a `sub sp` frame). sd_water scans up from the base for the first non-fill byte, which is robust. sd_cwater's result is banked as sd_rom08, 'the number that sizes SCH_CHSTK' (stkdiag.inc:713-714), and sd_mwater's sizes MOU_PSTK. Knob-only.
findings.recommendation: Scan bottom-up (cld / repe scasb from the base; depth = top - first non-sentinel), and re-take any field number that came from this panel.
findings.verify_note: Read both routines: std / repne scasb from top-1 for the first 0xE5, so an early match under-reports. The '~20%' chance assumes random bytes; real frames hold IPs, flags and F000 segments, so the odds are lower but non-zero, and gaps under-report regardless.

findings.title: The death panel trusts the table it calls suspect
findings.detail: sch_diepanel reads T_INST and, unless 0xFF, calls inst_ptr (which cbw's the index) and prints I_NAME with no bound on the index, though its own header says every record is suspect after an overrun; it also draws into whatever mode is live, including an fsx bracket's foreign mode.
findings.recommendation: Record. If touched: cmp al, INST_MAX / jae .name.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: no bound before `call inst_ptr`; an index >= 80h sign-extends below inst_tab and sch_dpstr prints until a NUL.

findings.title: Comment rot is the area's real defect
findings.detail: sched.inc is 3,092 lines for ~700 of code and its comments carry history ('it was X until size pass N'). Some fifteen statements in sched.inc alone describe replaced designs (multiply/shift canary, sch_stacks + slot*SCH_STACK in three places, the 256 path 'still there', kmain line numbers, .boot2 claims for an .ovl body, an orphaned sch_switch header after sch_clsbytes, a dangling fragment, 'all tasks run CS = DS = KERNEL_SEG'); stkdiag.inc has headers for routines that no longer exist. One stale statement is not a comment: the %error at sched.inc:121 ('it is the largest class and every class is one') is false since 192-byte classes exist, and the %if it guards protects nothing any more.
findings.recommendation: One pass that strips history from code comments (SPEC.md and plans hold it), keeps invariant + reason, and moves the sch_switch header above sch_switch:. Drop or re-word the sched.inc:121 %if/%error as a code change (not a comment fix).
findings.verify_note: Each cited line re-read; the comment-only fixes are in doc_fixes. The sched.inc:121 item was moved here from the doc list because it is an %error string, which a comment-only fix may not touch.

findings.title: fsx_rtick is a third copy of the chain swap and the hook guard
findings.detail: kern_mega's real-mode bracket ISR re-spells sch_isr's chain swap and sch_rhook's skip tests, including the same sti-before-the-tests shape (harmless there, since its skip path is the ISR's own exit), so fixes such as sched-7's chain canary do not reach it.
findings.recommendation: One macro for the swap/chain/restore and one for the hook guard, used at both sites.
findings.verify_note: Copy confirmed (fsx.inc:1382-1427). Corrected: sched-2's IF leak does not exist in fsx_rtick, whose .out path pops and irets, restoring the interrupted FLAGS.

findings.title: sched_init's zero stores rest on an unresolved contradiction about .bss
findings.detail: sched.inc and SPEC.md 8 say nothing clears .bss at boot; events.inc, blank.inc, dock.inc, memory.inc, SPEC.md 10 and SPEC.md 12.8.5.1 (which measured 0x00 on a live machine) say .bss arrives zeroed from the image padding. The scheduler itself already depends on the latter: nothing in the tree stores [sch_chbusy] before sch_isr's first test of it, and a non-zero byte there would skip every chain and refuse every switch. If .bss is zero, ~30 bytes of zero stores sit in kern_big's boot-overlay window, which is 5,119 of its 5,120-byte bound.
evidence: build/kernel-full.bin: 0 non-zero bytes over .bss's file span 0xB788..0xCC7E
findings.recommendation: Rule once in SPEC.md 2.6 (with a gate that the padding covers .bss on every kernel); then either keep the stores as deliberate and fix their comments, or drop them and give the overlay its room. Either way sch_chbusy needs a store or the rule.
findings.verify_note: Verified on build/kernel-full.bin that the bytes under .bss are padding and all zero on kern_big; found sch_chbusy is never initialised (kern_big's word store at sched.inc:337 covers sch_rbusy/sch_lock, and sch_chbusy is the byte below them). No gate asserting the padding was found. SPEC.md 8's sentence is fixed below to the measured state without pre-empting the ruling.

findings.title: evq_pop banks DS for a prefix hazard that cannot occur
findings.detail: The reason given ('the 8086 LOSES the prefix when a string op restarts') applies only to REP string instructions with an override; four unrepeated movsw cannot be interrupted mid-instruction. Four ss movsw are the same 4 bytes and ~35 clocks cheaper on the 8088 than push ds/push ss/pop ds/pop ds (52 clocks of segment push/pop against 4 x 3.78 for the prefixes).
evidence: SPEC.md:18180-18185 repeats it and still says rep movsw
findings.recommendation: Take the prefix form, or keep the banking and correct the reason in both places (doc fixes below do the latter).
findings.verify_note: Copy is push ds / push ss / pop ds / 4 x movsw / pop ds with no REP; the prefix-loss erratum needs an interrupted REP.

findings.title: sch_clsbytes row 0 duplicates row 4
findings.detail: Rows 0 and 4 are both SCH_STACK, and inst_pkg_spawn already maps an out-of-range index to CX=0 (task_spawn's 'largest'). A dec bx before the bound check makes 0 out of range and drops the row.
findings.recommendation: dec bx; cmp bx, SCH_NCLASS (with row 0 dropped); only if the file is open anyway. tests/unit/t_stkclass.py's CLASS_BYTES and tools/os88pkg.py's STK_CLASS_MAX mirror the index meanings, not the table, and need no change.
findings.verify_note: inst_pkg_spawn: `cmp bx, SCH_NCLASS / jae .havecls` with CX = 0 preset; 0 -> 0xFFFF after dec is out of range. Net: +1 (dec) -2 (row).

findings.title: A task can block only on time - there is no wait-on-anything primitive
findings.detail: Every non-time wait polls: the SB refill task wakes every tick to look, gfx_lock waiters stay READY and spin through task_yield, workers poll OSAPI_TASK_ALIVE, and sch_wake_ui is a one-task special case of the missing primitive. On an 8088 a poll that finds nothing still costs a switch in and out.
findings.recommendation: task_wake(AL=slot): if T_STATE==2 make it 1 and post sch_idlewake, else set a sticky wake-pending bit (T_FLAGS bit 1); task_sleep tests-and-clears it under its own cli and returns at once if set. ISR-safe, no record growth, plus a rare OSAPI cell appended at the end (additive, abilock --update without a PKG_FMT bump). Enables IRQ-driven SB refill, NIC-driven ETHER service, sched-16 and sched-17.
findings.prior_art: AmigaOS Exec Signal/Wait (one signal bit); Unix System V sleep(chan)/wakeup(chan) with the slot as channel; OS/2 DosSemWait
findings.verify_note: Premises re-read: sbl_refill_task sleeps 1 tick and polls; gfx_lock .block yields and retries; task_sleep has no pending-wake test today. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE. T_FLAGS bit 1 is free (only TF_SERVICE = bit 0 is defined).

findings.title: A UI wake gets no priority over ready workers
findings.detail: sch_switch scans round-robin from cur+1, so a UI task woken by input while two or more workers are runnable waits for the tick and then for every ready worker ahead of slot 0: up to N x 55 ms. SPEC.md 7.3 fixed the lock half of starvation and explicitly left 'the UI task does not run more often' open.
evidence: SPEC.md:18270 'This does not make the UI task run more often'
findings.recommendation: One-shot boost: sch_wake_ui sets [sch_uiboost] only when task 0 was sleeping; sch_switch spends it by picking slot 0 directly when task 0 is READY and fsx_task is 0xFF. One boost per sleep-to-wake bounds worker starvation to one UI pass per input. Measure first on MartyPC with two drawing workers using 7.3's breakpoint method.
findings.prior_art: OS/2 1.x foreground/IO boosts; GEOS UI thread above application threads; AmigaOS input handler at priority 20
findings.verify_note: Scan order confirmed (inc dl from [sch_cur], no priority). The quoted sentence is at SPEC.md:18270 (10.1), not in 7.3.

findings.title: gfx_lock waiters poll rather than block
findings.detail: A blocked waiter is READY and is switched in every round only to yield again - about two switches per waiter per tick for as long as the lock is held. With sched-15, .block could sleep with the pending bit armed and gfx_unlock could wake a recorded waiter; the 7.3 fairness handover would need re-proving.
evidence: SPEC.md:11710 'a real ticket lock wants a per-task wait word and a scheduler that can block on it'
findings.recommendation: Record until sched-15 exists and a measurement shows the spin matters.

findings.title: Exiting with sch_lock raised kills pre-emption for the session, and no contract says so
findings.detail: task_exit jumps into sch_switch without looking at sch_lock; the forced switch succeeds and the next task runs with pre-emption off and every yield a no-op for ever. inst_task_die, the normal road, does not hold it.
findings.recommendation: Write the rule on task_exit and in SPEC.md 8: a task may not exit with sch_lock raised.
findings.verify_note: task_exit (sched.inc:1189-1211) reads nothing of sch_lock and enters sch_switch, which does not test it either.

findings.title: 16-bit ticks bound every deadline at 30 minutes
findings.detail: [ticks], T_WAKE and OSAPI_GET_TICKS are 16-bit; Mac Ticks, Win16 GetTickCount and AmigaOS timer.device were 32-bit. A high word incremented on the carry is cheap; answering DX from OSAPI_GET_TICKS changes a register the cell may today preserve.
findings.recommendation: Record for the flag day only if a package asks; the RTC ladder covers long intervals today.
findings.verify_note: ticks is resw 1 and the cell is `out AX = [ticks]`.

doc_fixes.old_text:
- **The pop copy** — the other way round, and the one that cannot use a prefix.
  The source is the ring, and `rep movsw` reads it through DS: **the 8086 loses
  a segment prefix when a string instruction restarts after an interrupt**, and
  NMI reaches inside the `cli` this runs under. So DS is *banked* around the
  copy and restored, which is the rule §2.1 states and the only shape that is
  correct on the target.
doc_fixes.new_text:
- **The pop copy** — the other way round. The source is the ring, and four
  unrepeated `movsw` read it through DS, so DS is *banked* around the copy and
  restored. Four `ss` prefixes would be the same four bytes and as correct:
  the 8086 loses a segment prefix only when an interrupted `rep` string
  instruction restarts, and this copy has no `rep`.
doc_fixes.why: evq_pop's copy is push ds/push ss/pop ds, four movsw, pop ds (events.inc:264-271) - no REP, so no restart.

doc_fixes.new_text: `kern_big` has **twelve usable worker slots** and `kern_small` three.
doc_fixes.why: kern_small has four slices and the idle task holds its only 128 (sched.inc:196-204: 'THREE USABLE').

doc_fixes.old_text:
every size must be
a multiple of 128 and even,
doc_fixes.new_text:
every size must be
even (`SCH_SLOT`'s `%error`; only `SCH_STACK` is still held to a multiple of 128),
doc_fixes.why: SCH_SLOT checks evenness and >= SCH_FRAME + 2 only (sched.inc:251-256); 192-byte classes exist; only SCH_STACK has a %128 %error (120-122).

doc_fixes.old_text: ; Your worker gets DX = your instance index, DS = ES = CS = KERNEL_SEG,
doc_fixes.new_text:
; Your worker gets DX = your instance index, DS = CS = YOUR segment,
; ES = KERNEL_SEG,
doc_fixes.why: sch_frame writes the package segment into DS and CS and KERNEL_SEG into ES (sched.inc:1079-1104); SPEC.md 20.6 states the same. Column-0 comment: not in abilock's fingerprint.

doc_fixes.why: inst_pkg_spawn reads LD_H_CLASS and task_spawn takes the smallest free slice at least that big (instance.inc:2095-2111, sched.inc:930-937).
